filename: Deep Koopman operators for causal discovery.pdf
title: Deep Koopman operators for causal discovery
testbed_rationale: The focus of this paper is causal discovery and system identification in nonlinear dynamical systems and conceptual/reanalysis ENSO indices, not developing or benchmarking physics parameterizations or ESM emulators.
pain_points: Nonlinear causal inference typically valid only locally along trajectories, failing to generalize globally.
Nonlinearities, feedback loops, nonstationarity, and multiscale interactions break classical Granger causality assumptions.
High dimensionality limits classical constraint-based and statistical causal discovery methods (e.g., PCMCI+, VARLiNGAM).
Prescribed dictionary functions (like Random Fourier Features) struggle to capture complex nonlinear dynamics without deep neural network feature learning.
Sensitivity of deep Koopman learning to hyperparameter choices and risk of error magnification in marginal vs joint DMD models.
extraction_notes: LEAP STC acknowledged in the Acknowledgements (Award #2019625). The study introduces Kausal, combining deep representation learning of observables with dynamic mode decomposition to perform Granger causality in linearized latent spaces.
